isomorphisms.name: Constrained Optimization as Atonement Configuration
isomorphisms.domain_a: Physics: Constrained optimization in a one-dimensional parameter space with multiple inequality constraints
isomorphisms.domain_b: Theology: The Cross as the unique solution to the problem of moral cost, justice, and mercy
isomorphisms.chi_law: The unique feasible point in a constrained optimization problem corresponds to the unique atonement configuration that satisfies all divine and moral constraints.
isomorphisms.physics_process: Solving a constrained optimization problem: minimize or find feasible point in a one-dimensional parameter space (α ∈ [0,1]) subject to five inequality constraints (P1-P5) and one identity condition (judge = payer). The feasible set collapses to a single point.
isomorphisms.theological_phenomenon: The Cross as the unique configuration where judge pays full cost (α=0), satisfying conservation, irreversibility, externality, meta-level status, and record-preservation.
isomorphisms.prediction: Any alternative configuration (e.g., cost waived, offender self-pays, peer-level transfer, algorithmic resolution, cost destroyed) will violate at least one of the five constraints, leaving the Cross as the only feasible point.
physics_process_steps: Impose constraint P1 (Gödel): system cannot self-certify completeness.
Impose constraint P2 (Tarski): truth cannot be defined within the system.
Impose constraint P3 (Turing/Church): optimal α not computable from within.
Impose constraint P5 (Landauer): erasing record costs energy, does not eliminate cost.
Impose identity condition: payer must be judge.
Solve: feasible set = {α=0, payer=judge, payer external/meta-level}.
mapped_text_steps: Define α ∈ [0,1] for cost-sharing in resolution operator R(offense, α).
Surviving configuration: α=0, payer=judge, payer external, meta-level, anti-entropic, record-preserving.
preserved_transitions: From α=1 (Perfect Justice) to α=0 (Perfect Mercy) via constraints: the transition is forced, not arbitrary.
From five rival configurations to single survivor: each elimination step corresponds to a constraint violation.
missing_transitions: No missing transitions; all five elimination steps are explicitly mapped.
isomorphisms.notes: The mapping is exceptionally strong. The physics process (constrained optimization) and theological process (elimination of rival atonement theories) share identical logical structure: a one-dimensional parameter space, five independent constraints, and a unique feasible point. The identity condition (judge=payer) is an additional structural requirement not present in generic optimization but essential to the theological claim. The density score is high because every step in the physics process has a direct, one-to-one counterpart in the theological text.

isomorphisms.name: Conservation Law as Moral Ledger
isomorphisms.domain_a: Physics: Conservation of a quantity (e.g., energy, charge) in a closed system
isomorphisms.domain_b: Theology: Moral cost as a conserved quantity that cannot be waived or destroyed
isomorphisms.chi_law: A conserved quantity in physics corresponds to a moral cost that must be preserved and cannot be eliminated by decree.
isomorphisms.physics_process: Conservation law: dQ/dt = 0 for a closed system. The quantity Q cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred.
isomorphisms.theological_phenomenon: Moral cost (δ + ν_loss) is conserved; it cannot be waived (Configuration 1) or destroyed (Configuration 5). It must be borne by someone.
isomorphisms.prediction: Any attempt to eliminate the moral cost without a payer will violate the conservation law, leading to an unbalanced ledger.
physics_process_steps: Conclude Q cannot be destroyed; can only be transferred.
mapped_text_steps: Identify moral cost as conserved quantity (Page 05, Page 12).
Assert conservation law: Q_m is preserved (Page 12).
Conclude cost cannot be waived (Configuration 1) or destroyed (Configuration 5); must be paid by someone.
preserved_transitions: From conservation to impossibility of waiver: direct logical implication.
isomorphisms.notes: The mapping is direct and well-defined. The conservation law in physics (dQ/dt=0) maps exactly to the theological claim that moral cost cannot be eliminated. The only nuance is that the theological 'system' may include external payers, which is analogous to an open system in physics.

isomorphisms.name: Gödel's Incompleteness as Self-Repair Impossibility
isomorphisms.domain_a: Mathematics: Gödel's first incompleteness theorem — a sufficiently powerful formal system cannot prove its own consistency
isomorphisms.domain_b: Theology: The offender (inside the system) cannot certify that the moral debt is fully paid
isomorphisms.chi_law: The inability of a system to certify its own consistency corresponds to the inability of a moral agent to self-certify complete atonement.
isomorphisms.physics_process: Gödel's theorem is a mathematical/logical result, not a physics process. It is a formal constraint on provability.
isomorphisms.theological_phenomenon: Configuration 2 (offender self-pays) is eliminated because the offender cannot know when the debt is fully paid — requires stepping outside the system.
isomorphisms.prediction: Any self-payment scheme will be incomplete because the agent cannot certify finality.
physics_process_steps: Formal system S cannot prove its own consistency.
Any proof of consistency requires a meta-system.
mapped_text_steps: Offender is inside the moral system.
Offender cannot certify full payment of debt (requires meta-level perspective).
preserved_transitions: From internal to meta-level: both require stepping outside the system.
isomorphisms.notes: This is a structural isomorphism between a mathematical theorem and a theological claim. It is not a physics process, but the mapping is logically rigorous. The 'does_mirror_physics_process' is false because Gödel's theorem is not physics, but the mapping is still valid as a formal constraint.

isomorphisms.name: Landauer's Principle as Record-Preservation
isomorphisms.domain_a: Physics: Landauer's principle — erasing one bit of information requires dissipating at least kT ln 2 energy
isomorphisms.domain_b: Theology: Destroying the moral record (amnesia) does not eliminate the cost; it merely moves it and loses information
isomorphisms.chi_law: The thermodynamic cost of erasing information corresponds to the impossibility of eliminating moral cost by destroying the record.
isomorphisms.physics_process: Landauer's principle: erasing a bit costs energy kT ln 2; information is not destroyed for free.
isomorphisms.theological_phenomenon: Configuration 5 (cost destroyed by erasing the record) is eliminated because erasing costs energy and loses information that prevents recurrence.
isomorphisms.prediction: Erasing the moral record does not eliminate the cost; it merely transforms it and loses information.
physics_process_steps: Identify bit of information to be erased.
Conclude information is not destroyed for free; cost is transferred to environment.
mapped_text_steps: Identify moral record to be erased.
Recognize that erasing costs energy (moves cost, does not eliminate).
Conclude that erasing loses information that prevents recurrence.
preserved_transitions: From erasure to cost transfer: both involve moving rather than eliminating cost.
isomorphisms.notes: The mapping is direct and well-supported. Landauer's principle is a physics process, and the theological claim mirrors it closely. The only difference is that the theological 'cost' is moral rather than thermodynamic, but the structural role is identical.

isomorphisms.name: Turing/Church Undecidability as Optimal α Uncomputability
isomorphisms.domain_a: Computer Science: The halting problem is undecidable; there is no algorithm to determine whether an arbitrary program halts
isomorphisms.domain_b: Theology: No algorithm can determine the exact α that closes every ledger entry across all time
isomorphisms.chi_law: The undecidability of a computational problem corresponds to the impossibility of algorithmically determining the exact atonement parameter.
isomorphisms.physics_process: Turing/Church results are about computability, not physics processes. They are formal constraints on algorithms.
isomorphisms.theological_phenomenon: Configuration 4 (algorithmic resolution) is eliminated because the complete repair is not computable from within.
isomorphisms.prediction: No finite algorithm can compute the exact α that satisfies all constraints across all time.
physics_process_steps: Define computational problem: determine if program halts.
Prove no algorithm can solve for all programs.
mapped_text_steps: Define problem: compute optimal α that closes all ledger entries.
Argue that no algorithm from within the system can do this.
preserved_transitions: From problem definition to impossibility proof: both follow the same logical structure.
isomorphisms.notes: Again, this is a formal constraint rather than a physics process, but the structural isomorphism is clear. The mapping is one-to-one at the level of logical structure.
